# Pattern Bank

The synthesis plus outlier evidence from the creator's pattern research. The entry point for `vid-framing` when picking an angle. Sub-banks for power words and title shapes live in their own files (loaded by `vid-title`). Thumbnail strategy and visual data live IN the outlier rows below.

> [!info] How this set was built
> Last 12 months. Three circles: own channel, 3 direct competitors, 5 adjacent channels, plus 3 style-only giants mined for packaging shape only (never topics). Each channel's outlier floor is scaled to its size, not a flat 2x, so a 600k video counts as a flop for NetworkChuck and a breakout for Nicky.

## Sub-banks (focused, loaded by writing skills)

- [[title-bank]]: fill-in-the-blank title shapes with worked examples, loaded by `vid-title`
- [[power-words-bank]]: global + audience-specific power words, loaded by `vid-title`

## Synthesis (cross-channel insights)

The "what we learned" layer. `vid-framing` reads this first when picking angles; the outlier rows below are the evidence.

> [!important] The split that matters most for you
> The strongest, most convergent patterns in this set fall into two off-lane buckets: **tool-news jacking** ("[Tool] Just Dropped, And It Kills [X]") and **make money with AI** ("$0 to $1M," "Make $15k in 10 Days"). They print views, but they are not your lane and they age the moment the tool does. Your lane (AI amplifying an expert's content, voice intact, creator in charge) shows up in a smaller, higher-fit cluster: **AI builds your team while you stay in control**, **create real content fast**, and **contrarian creator takes**. The curation pass is about keeping the on-lane gold and consciously deciding how much off-lane reach you are willing to borrow.

> [!important] Convergent patterns (proven across the most channels)
> Appear across multiple channels and across circles. Test these first.
>
> 1. **Speed-to-outcome compression** `[Skill/Tool] in [N] Minutes` / `Learn 80% of [X] in Under [N] Minutes`. The single most convergent shape in the set: Brock, Nicky, Nate, Jeff, Tina, Duncan. ON-LANE (e.g. "Build your whole content team in 20 minutes").
> 2. **New-tool news jacking** `[Tool] Just Dropped (And It Kills/Changes [X])` / `[Tool] Just Changed [Activity] Forever`. Huge frequency across Brock, Nick, Nate, Sabrina, Ed. OFF-LANE by default (tool-chasing, fast decay). The one survivable variant is "Just Changed Content Creation Forever," used sparingly.
> 3. **Mastery vs the crowd** `How to Use [X] Better Than 99% of People` / `[N]% of People [Do X] Wrong`. Brock, Duncan, Ondrej, Jeff. ON-LANE.
> 4. **"Steal this" generosity** `[N] [Tool] Skills/Prompts ... (steal them)`. Brock, Nate, Sabrina, Duncan, Tina. ON-LANE.

> [!note] Niche-specific patterns (strong for YOUR audience)
> Appear in the direct set. Lower raw frequency, highest strategic fit.
>
> 1. **AI builds your team, you keep control** `I Built My Entire [Content] Team Inside Claude (No Employees)`. Nicky (x2), Duncan, Brock ("Build an AI Employee"). This is the most on-lane pattern in the entire set: AI as amplifier, no slop, creator in charge.
> 2. **Create real content fast with a named tool** `How I Use [VEO/Sora/Claude] To Create Viral [Content] In [N] Minutes`. Nicky (x3). Direct, on-lane.
> 3. **Exact systems that convert** `The EXACT System To [revenue outcome] (In [time])`. Ed. Speaks to business owners who measure content by money, not vanity.
> 4. **Contrarian creator takes** `Why [counterintuitive creator claim] (Nobody Talks About This)`. Nicky ("Introverts Make the BEST Content Creators"), Ed ("Personal Brand Is An AWFUL Idea"). Differentiating, on-lane.

> [!tip] Adjacent translations (differentiation gold, structure only)
> Shapes from adjacent channels not yet used in your exact lane. Take the shape, never the topic.
>
> 1. **Contrarian command** `DON'T [common practice], [do Y] instead`. Duncan, Nate, Nick. Transfers cleanly as a content take.
> 2. **Versus / death framing** `[Tool] Kills/Destroys [Category]`. Nick, Nate, Ondrej. Aggressive; flag for tone fit.
> 3. **Definitive long course** `Build & Sell [X] (N-Hour Course)`. Nate, Nick. Topic is automation (do not take it); the "one definitive flagship" packaging could translate to a cornerstone content video.
> 4. **Dollar-and-timeframe specificity** `$0 to $1M` / `Make $X in N Days`. Sabrina, Nate. Topic (make money with AI) is OFF your lane. The specific-number + timeframe structure transfers only if you ever show a real content ROI.

> [!warning] Channel-unique signals (one channel only)
> 1. Ed's `Copy This [asset], It'll Blow Up Your Business`. Ed only, but proven repeatedly for him.
> 2. NetworkChuck's `you need [X] RIGHT NOW!!` hype cadence. His energy; style reference only.
> 3. Sabrina's `So Well It Feels Illegal` / `The Laziest Way`. Her voice; low transfer to yours.

### Topic clusters (own + direct only, never adjacent)

What the direct audience clicks on, by subject. Adjacent topics deliberately excluded.

> [!abstract] Cluster 1: The AI content-creation toolchain
> VEO, Sora, ChatGPT Images, Higgsfield, Claude Video used to make real content fast.
> Members: Nicky's VEO 3 / VEO 3.1 / Sora 2 / Higgsfield videos, Brock "Claude Video Just Changed Content Creation."
> Why it pulls: creators want to produce real content faster without sounding like a machine.

> [!abstract] Cluster 2: The AI team with no staff
> Members: Nicky "Content Team Inside Claude," "4 AI Teams (No Employees)"; Brock "Build an AI Employee"; Duncan "Built My ENTIRE Marketing Team."
> Why it pulls: solo experts want leverage without hiring, and without handing their voice to a stranger.

> [!abstract] Cluster 3: Claude mastery for non-technical business owners
> Members: Brock "Better Than 99% of People," "for Normal People," "Claude for Small Businesses."
> Why it pulls: business owners want the powerful tool without having to become technical.

> [!abstract] Cluster 4: Content that turns views into revenue (and AI disrupting it)
> Members: Ed "EXACT System To [revenue]," "Blow Up Your Business," "Businesses On YouTube Have A BIG AI Problem," "$1M from YouTube Using AI."
> Why it pulls: the business-owner audience measures content by outcome, not vanity metrics.

> [!abstract] Cluster 5: Contrarian creator psychology
> Members: Nicky "Introverts Make the BEST Content Creators," Ed "Growing A Personal Brand Is An AWFUL Idea," "I QUIT social media & grew my business."
> Why it pulls: pattern-interrupt takes that still serve the creator's identity, not empty contrarianism.

> [!tip] Thumbnail convergence (17 top performers classified)
> The niche speaks one visual language. **Minimal dominates** (about 10 of 17): an oversized white sans-serif claim of 3 to 4 words, a dark or clean background, and one accent color, almost always **Claude orange**, with the creator's face and a clear expression (or a clean logo/infographic and no face, like Brock). The hooks that layer on top of Minimal are **Curiosity** ("NOBODY TELLS YOU THIS", mouths taped shut), **Cognitive Dissonance** ("STOP PAYING FOR SORA"), and **Result** (cash props, a 1.2M view badge, cinematic AI outputs on display). The big course channels (Nate, Nick) use a **whiteboard-curriculum** variant: a hand-drawn numbered list and an architecture diagram beside the face, which is the proven shape for a definitive cornerstone piece.
>
> The takeaways for your packaging: lead with **Minimal** (huge legible claim, dark + Claude-orange, your face with a real expression, 4 words or fewer), and keep a **Curiosity / Cognitive Dissonance** hook in your pocket for the contrarian and borrow-with-care videos. Save the whiteboard-curriculum look for a quarterly cornerstone.

## Field reference
